title: Luma effects review
scope: Catalog and renderer review of the editor used by these workshops. The review describes implemented behavior; it is not a certification of every device or Photoshop interchange case.
recommendation: Start with Multiply, Screen, Soft Light, Stroke, Drop Shadow and a small Gaussian Blur. Then introduce Blend If, filter order, and backdrop-dependent effects.

effects.label: Bevel & Emboss
effects.purpose: Give lettering a raised or engraved edge.
effects.exercise: Try on the headline; adjust depth, lighting and highlight/shadow colors.
effects.boundary: A 2D layer style, separate from Luma’s editable 3D lettering.

effects.label: Stroke
effects.exercise: A thin contrasting stroke keeps the headline readable over busy imagery.
effects.boundary: Inside, outside and center placement; color, gradient and pattern fills.

effects.label: Inner Shadow
effects.purpose: Shade the inside edge of a layer.
effects.exercise: Use a small offset for inset lettering or a paper-cut impression.
effects.boundary: Works from the layer’s silhouette; it does not infer scene geometry.

effects.label: Inner Glow
effects.exercise: Try a restrained highlight on the character or title.
effects.boundary: Supports edge/center source and softer/precise falloff.

effects.label: Satin
effects.purpose: Add overlapping, shaded ripples inside a layer.
effects.exercise: Explore on large lettering where the contour is easy to see.
effects.boundary: A graphic shading treatment; it does not simulate fabric.

effects.label: Color Overlay
effects.purpose: Cover a layer’s visible content with a color treatment.
effects.exercise: Try a colored motif and compare the effect’s own blend modes.
effects.boundary: An overlay is different from selecting and replacing particular source colors.

effects.label: Gradient Overlay
effects.purpose: Apply a gradient within a layer.
effects.exercise: Give the title a two-color finish, then change gradient direction.
effects.boundary: Linear, radial, angle, reflected and diamond gradients.

effects.label: Pattern Overlay
effects.purpose: Fill the silhouette with a repeated pattern.
effects.exercise: Try dots or stripes on the headline.
effects.boundary: The current style offers checker, stripes and dots; custom image brushes are a separate tool.

effects.label: Bloom
effects.purpose: Spread a glow from bright source pixels.
effects.exercise: Try low opacity on the light wash or a bright image.
effects.boundary: Threshold controls which highlights contribute; dark layers may show little change.

effects.label: Relief
effects.purpose: Shade according to the layer’s image detail.
effects.exercise: Try on the fabric motif for a pressed texture.
effects.boundary: Image-based 2D shading, without editable geometric depth.

effects.label: Outer Glow
effects.purpose: Add a halo beyond the layer edge.
effects.exercise: Try behind the headline against a dark scene.
effects.boundary: Its appearance depends on the silhouette and contrast with the background.

effects.label: Drop Shadow
effects.purpose: Offset a soft silhouette behind a layer.
effects.exercise: Start here for readable type and separated collage panels.
effects.boundary: The current below-content effect does not offer backdrop blend-mode control.

effects.label: Long Shadow
effects.purpose: Extend the silhouette along an offset.
effects.exercise: Use on a short headline for a bold graphic direction.

effects.label: Contact Shadow
effects.purpose: Add localized darkening around the layer’s contact region.
effects.exercise: Compare at low opacity on an overlapping image.
effects.boundary: A compositing treatment; it does not calculate physical contact with 3D geometry.

effects.label: Backdrop Blur
effects.purpose: Blur the layers behind the selected silhouette.
effects.exercise: Try on the collage or headline above a detailed scene.
effects.boundary: Needs visible content underneath. It blurs the backdrop, not the selected layer’s own pixels.

effects.label: Refraction
effects.purpose: Distort the backdrop around the selected silhouette’s alpha edges.
effects.exercise: Use above the scene for a glass-like edge treatment.
effects.boundary: A 2D alpha-driven approximation, not physically accurate glass.

effects.label: Reflection
effects.purpose: Mirror the backdrop inside the selected layer’s silhouette.
effects.exercise: Adjust offset and blur to explore what appears inside the shape.
effects.boundary: Reflects the backdrop around the layer center; it is not an automatic floor reflection of the object.

filters.label: Gaussian Blur
filters.purpose: Soften detail and separate a busy background from the subject.
filters.boundary: Start with 2–4 px; the Gaussian-style blur uses a three-pass box approximation.

filters.label: Motion Blur
filters.purpose: Smear detail along a chosen direction.
filters.boundary: Use modest radius and angle for an intentional motion study.

filters.label: Surface Blur
filters.purpose: Smooth neighboring colors while retaining stronger edges.
filters.boundary: Radius and threshold trade texture against edge preservation.

filters.label: Unsharp Mask
filters.purpose: Increase edge contrast with Unsharp Mask.
filters.boundary: Inspect at full size; too much amount creates halos.

filters.label: High Pass
filters.purpose: Isolate edge detail around middle gray.
filters.boundary: Pair with Overlay or Soft Light; Normal intentionally looks gray.

filters.label: Median
filters.purpose: Replace isolated pixel values with neighborhood medians.
filters.boundary: Useful for a small cleanup study; large values remove detail.

filters.label: Dust & Scratches
filters.purpose: Replace sufficiently different pixels with a neighborhood median.
filters.boundary: Threshold and radius need close inspection on the actual source.

filters.label: Reduce Noise
filters.purpose: Smooth luminance and color noise with separate controls.
filters.boundary: Compare texture before and after; this is a local denoise filter.

filters.label: Lens Blur
filters.purpose: Use an aperture-shaped blur with highlight bloom.
filters.boundary: Blades, rotation and highlights change the look; it does not infer a depth map.

filters.label: Displace
filters.purpose: Ripple pixels using an adjustable wave.
filters.boundary: The current filter is procedural-wave displacement, not an uploaded displacement-map workflow.

filters.label: Maximum
filters.boundary: A morphology-style effect; can make fine artwork look heavier or lighter depending on polarity.

filters.label: Minimum
filters.boundary: Compare with Maximum on the motif to understand the difference.

filters.label: Invert
filters.boundary: Useful for a negative treatment or dramatic blend experiment.

filters.label: Desaturate
filters.boundary: Adjust the amount or filter opacity to retain some color.

filters.label: Hue Rotate
filters.boundary: White and gray contain little hue; use targeted Recolor for the white-shirt lesson.

blends.description: Normal stacks pixels directly; Dissolve distributes partial opacity as a stippled pattern.
Favor darker values. Start with Multiply for ink and texture.
Favor lighter values. Start with Screen for light, fog and glow.
Combine darkening and lightening. Start with Soft Light, then compare Overlay.
Create differences, negatives and strong graphic interactions. Useful for experimentation and image comparison.
Take hue, saturation, color or luminosity from a layer while combining the remaining components with its backdrop.

recipes.label: Detail
recipes.description: Crisp local contrast without a hard-edged sharpen

recipes.label: Glow
recipes.description: Broad luminous lift with a restrained highlight bloom

recipes.label: Depth
recipes.description: Deepen form while preserving highlight separation

recipes.label: Color
recipes.description: Transfer chroma while retaining underlying luminosity

recipes.label: Cinema
recipes.description: Dense contrast, soft highlight rolloff, controlled color

notes: Layer effects style a layer’s content or silhouette. Smart filters process its image. Blend modes combine it with the layers below. Adjustment layers change color or tone across the layers they affect.
Effects and filters can be edited, disabled, reordered and undone. Several effects depend on content beneath them; use the eight-layer project for meaningful comparisons.
Blend If offers source and underlying tonal ranges with feathered transitions. Multiple blend passes and the five recipes are advanced blending features, not additional blend modes.
Keep the eight-layer exercise intact: explore adjustment layers in a duplicate project because adding one creates another layer.
Pressure-based retouching and authenticated generative edits are separate workflows. They are not counted as local effects in this catalog.
Save an editable .luma master. Photoshop export preserves supported results with conversion warnings; native editable equivalence is not promised for every Luma effect or smart filter.
